{{Quote|Sometimes one must turn the soil to save the garden|Momaw Nadon|<ref name="GG7" />}}
'''Momaw Nadon''' was an [[Ithorian/Legends|Ithorian]] who was exiled from his homeworld, [[Ithor/Legends|Ithor]], after he revealed secrets of Ithorian agricultural technology to the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. He spent much of his exile on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], and was present in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Cantina]] when [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] came searching for passage to [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].

==Biography==
===Ithorian exile===
Momaw Nadon, an [[Ithorian/Legends|Ithorian]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Scholar/Legends|scholar]],<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|momawnadon|Nadon, Momaw}}</ref> was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]]<ref name="FF33" /> on his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ithor/Legends|Ithor]].<ref name="DB" /> For many [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]], he served as a [[High Priest/Legends|High Priest]] and a leader of<ref name="The Sand Tender: The Hammerhead's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=The Sand Tender: The Hammerhead's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref> the famous<ref name="FF33" /> [[Ithorian Herdship]] ''[[Tafanda Bay]]''. During the early days of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]],<ref name="GalaxyGuide1" /> Nadon married his [[Marriage/Legends|wife]] [[Fandomar Nadon|Fandomar]], with whom he had a child. Shortly after their marriage,<ref name="The Sand Tender: The Hammerhead's Tale" /> [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] activity around Ithorian space brought the Imperial [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] ''[[Conquest (Imperial-class)/Legends|Conquest]]'' to his homeworld. [[Alima]], [[Captain/Legends|captain]] of the starship, attempted to infiltrate ''Tafanda Bay'' with spies, but failed in his endeavor, causing him to threaten Ithor's [[Mother Jungle/Legends|Mother Jungle]].<ref name="DB" /> For months, the Ithorians were subject to intense interrogation and scrutiny.<ref name="GalaxyGuide1" />

After eventually boarding the herdship, Alima demanded to know the secrets of Ithorian agricultural ceremonies, but Nadon refused to tell. The Imperial then had the Star Destroyer's weapons turned on the [[Cathor Hills]], a [[Tree/Legends|forest]] home to thousands of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Bafforr tree|Bafforr trees]] that had been Nadon's friends and teachers when he was young.<ref name="The Sand Tender: The Hammerhead's Tale" /> The herd leader viewed his choices as limited. He found had no choice but to give Alima what he wanted,<ref name="GalaxyGuide1" /> yet the captain opted to destroy the Mother Jungle. The weapons were then turned to Tafanda Bay and Alima ordered Nadon to surrender. In an attempt to save his people, the priest relinquished the secrets to the Imperial.<ref name="The Sand Tender: The Hammerhead's Tale" /> Nadon was put on trial, during which he gave a speech where he told the [[Council of Ithorian Elders]] he was guilty of sin against the hills, but that Ithor must not remain guilty in the sin of compliance to the Empire. The herd leader's answer was hard for the council to digest. The council put the matter high on the agenda for their next [[Herd Meet/Legends|Herd Meet]], though one would not occur for the next three [[Standard year/Legends|years]].<ref name="GalaxyGuide1" />

Nadon was excommunicated<ref name="DB" /> and banished him from Ithor<ref name="The Sand Tender: The Hammerhead's Tale" /> for at least three years,<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|355|Nadon, Momaw}}</ref> telling him to consider his evil actions in solitude. As he was banished<ref name="The Sand Tender: The Hammerhead's Tale" /> and forced to leave behind Fandomar and the rest of his family,<ref name="CSWE" /> his wife embraced him and told him she would wait for him should he ever return.<ref name="The Sand Tender: The Hammerhead's Tale" /> After his deportation, the Ithorian wandered across [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]], landing on the [[City/Legends|city]] [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], where he settled for some [[Time/Legends|time]].<ref name="GalaxyGuide1" />

===Tatooine===
[[File:TheGardenersSecret-GA.png|thumb|left|300px|Momaw Nadon secret garden outside Mos Eisley]]
While he was there, Nadon still honored the Ithorian traditions and tried to adapt large trees from [[Ithor/Legends|Ithor]] to the hot dry weather on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. He tended a [[Mos Eisley bafforr grove|first grove]] in his [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] [[Momaw Nadon's house|home]], including a carnivorous [[Vesuvague tree]]. The grove concealed a shelter where Momaw could hide [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] operatives fleeing the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. He also tended a [[Nadon's grove|second grove]] in the mountains south of Mos Eisley.

He met and fell in love with the fellow Ithorian, [[Slag Flats]] who was later killed by [[Jodo Kast]].<ref name="GG7">''[[Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley]]''</ref>

Around [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]] Nadon was wanted for espionage, and a security alert for him was displayed in places such as [[Spaceport THX1138]].<ref name="Star Tours 2">''[[Star Tours: The Adventures Continue]]''</ref>

While on Tatooine, he met up with Alima, who had been demoted to a [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]]. Alima threatened his [[bafforr tree]]s with death if he did not help him in finding an [[R2-D2/Legends|astromech]] the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]] was seeking. The pacifistic Nadon got so concerned about this, that he even tried to kill Alima. However, the attempt failed due to Nadon's lack of experience with weapons and Nadon was humiliated by Alima once more.

Finally, Nadon discovered the truth when he saw [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Cantina]]: The old man tried to smuggle the sought droid from Tatooine. Nadon then hid in the background when [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] tried to stop the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] from escaping. After having lost the droids, the Imperial Prefect searched for a scapegoat he could blame for this failure. Nadon then appeared on the scene and told the Imperial Prefect that he had informed Lieutenant Alima that the droids were leaving from this hangar two days before, and Alima was shot dead before he could protest. Horrified, Nadon took two cell samples from Alima's corpse. In keeping with the [[Law of Life]], Nadon made two clones, so that Alima would pay his debt to the Ithorians&mdash;and Nadon would pay his to Alima.<ref name="The Sand Tender: The Hammerhead's Tale" />

===Redemption===
{{Quote|I am Momaw Nadon, and I am honored to be of service to you, Wedge Antilles and Qwi Xux.''"''<br />''"''How do you know our names?''"''<br />''"''Mon Mothma asked me to give you special accommodations.|Momaw Nadon and Wedge Antillies|<ref name="Dark Apprentice novel">[[Dark Apprentice (novel)|''Dark Apprentice'']]</ref>}}
[[File:MomawNadonsHouse-TERC.png|thumb|right|250px|Nadon is held at gunpoint in his own home.]]
After a "great meet" of Ithorian Herd Ships, it was decided Nadon had acted with the best interest of the Ithorian people. His exile was ended, and he was restored as herd leader of ''Tafanda Bay''. Despite this restoration, Nadon still believed he had brought shame upon himself and vowed to spend the rest of his life accounting for his mistake. He was the representative when [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] brought [[Qwi Xux]] to Ithor, providing them with information on his lush homeworld.<ref name="Dark Apprentice novel" />

===Yuuzhan Vong War===
By [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], he had been replaced as the high priest and leader of the Ithorian people by [[Relal Tawron]]. On Ithor, he had a wife and son, [[Fandomar Nadon|Fandomar]] and [[Do-Forow Nadon]].

==Personality and traits==
Both Nadon's first name and surname hailed from Ithorian culture. His first name translated to "moonlight," while his last meant "tender, caretaker," referring to gardening.<ref name="Galactic Campaign Guide">''[[Galactic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> With brown [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]<ref name="EGC" /> and skin,<ref name="GG7" /> he stood at 1.95 [[Meter/Legends|meters]]<ref name="DB" /> and weighed 90 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]].<ref name="H2H" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Apparently everyone was cracking up, because it looked like a lush who was trying to get his drink and couldn't quite make it.|Jon Berg on the Hammerhead puppet|<ref name="Archives">''[[The Star Wars Archives: Episodes IV–VI, 1977–1983]]</ref>}}Momaw Nadon, originally referred to as Hammerhead,<ref name="Archives" /> was created for the [[original trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. The character was designed by conceptual artist [[Ron Cobb]] who, in notes, wrote that the character was a gentle aquatic creature that fed on plankton<ref name="DB" /> through bearing water through their mouth slits and out their lower "neck" openings. The brain of the character was located on a hump at the base of their neck, and their face, with simple and hunting eyes, lurched forward when doing long distance swimming.<ref name="NewSW.com">{{SW|url=news/from-a-certain-point-of-view-which-is-the-best-alien-species-in-star-wars|text=From a Certain Point of View: What is the Best Alien Design in ''Star Wars''?|nolive=1}}</ref> They practiced a religion based on tying and untying knots in cord and had a voice box implanted in in their chest.<ref name="DB" />  

Special effects artist [[Jon Berg]] built the Hammerhead mold<ref name="Chronicles">''[[Star Wars Chronicles]]''</ref> from couch foam and duct tape. Originally, the puppet had a mechanism where the head could move forward, but the finished puppet only had mechanisms to make the eyes blink and lights inside the eyes.<ref name="Archeology">{{YouTube|video=ElyMaaAFLKU|text=The Star Wars Cantina PT. 2 &#124; Full Panel #indianacomicconvention #tomspinadesigns #starwarshistory|channel=@FanXComicConventions|name=FanX Comic Conventions|date=2025-05-03}}</ref> Nadon was added to the film during supplemental shots for the cantina scene filmed at Dovington's Hollywood Studio between [[January 24]] and [[January 25]], [[1977]].<ref name="MakingOf">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref> Berg and [[Phil Tippett]] operated the Hammerhead puppet,<ref name="Archeology" /> and film director [[George Lucas]] helped set the puppet up.<ref name="Archives" /> Right before shooting, the side of the puppets head tore, though camera work hid this.<ref name="Archeology" /> During a scene where Berg used the character's arm to pull a glass toward themselves, the arms did not work, causing everyone at the studio to laugh.<ref name="Archives" /> The film, which marked Nadon's first appearance,<ref name="ANewHope">{{Film|IV}}</ref> released on [[May 25]], 1977.<ref name="Year">''[[Star Wars Year by Year: A Visual Chronicle]]''</ref>

Nadon was first publicly identified as Hammerhead in [[1978]] with the release of an action figure of the character from toy company [[Kenner Products|Kenner]].<ref name="Kenner">{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars (Kenner toy line)|pack=Hammerhead|link=VINtHammerhead.asp}}</ref> That year, Lucas's film production company [[Lucasfilm]] gave the character the name "Ammerha," though this went unused<ref name="CRC">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}</ref> and was overruled in [[1989]] with the publication of ''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]'', a supplement written by [[Grant S. Boucher]] for [[West End Games|West End Games's]] ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''. The guide was the first media to give the character the name "Momaw Nadon."<ref name="GalaxyGuide1">''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]''</ref>
